name: Bahia Palace
hero_subtitle: Painted ceilings, marble courtyards and orange trees: a palace built to impress.

overview.title: A Palace Built to Impress
overview.p1: Bahia means 'the beautiful', and the name is anything but modest. The palace was built in the late 19th century for the vizier Si Moussa and later expanded by his son Bou Ahmed, who wanted a residence that would outshine everything else in the city.
overview.p2: Inside you'll find the craft of the period at its best: painted cedar ceilings, carved stucco, zellige floors and a big marble courtyard with arcades, one of the most photographed corners of Marrakech. Only part of the complex is open, but it is plenty. Come early, before the tour groups fill the narrow passages.

moods.title: What to Look For at Bahia Palace
moods.subtitle: Three details that are easy to walk past.

1.title: Painted Cedar Ceilings
1.desc: Look up in almost every room. The patterns are hand-painted on cedar and still glow with reds, greens and gold.

2.title: The Marble Courtyard
2.desc: The main courtyard is the showpiece, surrounded by arcades and pleasantly cool even in summer. It is also where crowds gather, so go early.

3.title: Orange and Jasmine Courts
3.desc: Smaller garden courtyards are planted with orange and jasmine trees. They are the quietest corners to sit down and cool off.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Bahia Palace

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Walk from Jemaa el-Fnaa in about 20 minutes, or take a petit taxi and ask for the meter. The entrance is on Rue Riad Zitoun el Jdid.

2.title: Timing
2.desc: Open daily, roughly 9:00 to 17:00. Arrive at opening to avoid tour groups and the midday heat, and check current hours before you go.

3.title: Good to Know
3.desc: There is little signage inside, so a short guide or an audio walk helps. Pair it with El Badi Palace and the Saadian Tombs, both a short walk away.

q1.question: How long do you need at Bahia Palace?
q1.answer: Plan on 1 to 2 hours. The visit is a loop through courtyards and reception rooms, so you can go faster, but it rewards slow looking.

q2.question: Is Bahia Palace worth visiting?
q2.answer: Yes, if you like architecture and craft. It is the easiest place in the medina to see painted ceilings, zellige and carved stucco in one visit.

q3.question: How much is the entrance ticket?
q3.answer: Around 70 MAD, paid at the entrance. Prices and hours can change, so check locally before your visit.

q4.question: Can you visit Bahia Palace and El Badi Palace on the same day?
q4.answer: Yes, they are a short walk apart. Do Bahia in the morning, have lunch nearby, then visit El Badi in the afternoon.
